title: Fix fragmented function-callback JSON split across streaming chunks impacting VPC/Dedicated customers
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Multiple customers (one enterprise VPC customer + two Dedicated tenants) reported production failures where the server returned a valid function-callback payload but the SDK/consumer could not parse the JSON because the callback body was split across streaming chunks. This manifests as JSONSyntaxError/StructuredParse failures in downstream apps and causes automated workflows to abort. Issue appears in both Hosted->edge streaming paths and Dedicated/Private runtimes when there is aggressive chunking combined with KV cache re-entry and certain kernel scheduling patterns.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a long-running function-callback response (>2k characters) with nested JSON output and streaming enabled
2) Send the request via SDK with streaming=true and enable prefix/KV cache on the same model session

3) Observe that server emits the function-callback across multiple SSE/stream frames; intentionally trigger small chunk sizes by setting runtime batching/execution window to low values in Dedicated/VPC
4) Recreate consumer behaviour by concatenating frames naively without looking for escape sequences — parser fails with partial JSON errors in ~10-15% of runs
5) Verify in logs that chunk boundary splits occur mid-string/inside escape sequences and that the runtime's streaming framing lacks robust reassembly hints
investigation_summary: Triage began after an escalation from a VPC customer on 2026-03-09. We reproduced locally by forcing small streaming chunks and KV cache re-entry. Root cause is twofold: (A) runtime changes that introduced opportunistic chunk flushing for lower latency can split JSON tokens across frames, and (B) the SDK streaming layer assumes each 'data' event contains JSON-parsable units for function-callbacks, which is not a safe assumption for arbitrarily chunked streams. Additional amplification occurs in Dedicated because of a custom network MTU path in their private network and our continuous batching logic which merges segments in a way that can cut strings mid-escape. Logs attached in related_links show repeated "unexpected end of JSON input" patterns correlated with chunk boundary timestamps.
root_cause: Combined runtime chunk-flush behavior + SDK consumer assumptions. The runtime produced valid sequential bytes, but consumers attempted to parse per-frame rather than assembling full payloads. Dedicated/VPC networking and KV cache re-entry schedules increased probability of splitting inside JSON tokens.
mitigation: 1) Hotfix runtime to avoid flushing mid-UTF8 codepoint / inside JSON escape sequences for function-callback payloads (patch runtime streaming serializer to be token-aware)
2) Publish SDK patch that buffers stream frames for function-callback events until a complete JSON object can be decoded (backwards-compatible: small buffer with size cap + fallback timeout)
3) Apply customer-side mitigation guidance: set streaming buffer SDK flag or temporarily disable streaming for workflows that require strict JSON atom parsing
4) For Dedicated/VPC customers, propose a network-level MTU recommendation and a transient config to relax batching thresholds while hotfix deploys
rollout_plan: Day 0: merge runtime token-aware streaming serializer into canary runtime (internal build) and release to Canary pool in staging
Day 1: deploy SDK patch (npm/pypi) as 2.3.1-beta and notify customer engineering leads with integration instructions
Day 2: if canary stable for 3 hours of production-equivalent traffic, deploy runtime fix to Dedicated control plane and push hotfix to Hosted API routes behind feature flag
Day 3: coordinate Dedicated tenant patch windows for VPC customers (maintenance slot) and roll out SDK final release
Post-release: monitor parsing error rate and customer callbacks for 72 hours; rollback plan prepared if error rate rises
qa_checks: Unit tests: serializer should never split inside JSON string escape sequences or multi-byte UTF8 chars
Integration: end-to-end streaming test with artificial small-chunk emitter reproduces previous failure before patch and succeeds after
Load test: verify Dedicated autoscaling + KV cache re-entry under heavy concurrent sessions doesn't reintroduce split behavior
SDK tests: ensure streaming buffer flush timeout behaves correctly and does not break low-latency consumers
Security: confirm patch doesn't leak additional data across sessions or change access controls
